toes.note: Measured on the side sheet's near hand: wrist to toe tips about 0.46 (px 515 to 369), 0.12 deep at the knuckles. From the front (How to Draw, the SE poster, the GN cover): a broad hand, the four fingers thick and close together like a lizard's or a raptor's, fused into one mass at the palm and parted by grooves toward the tips; each finger three segments, rising to a knuckle bump and arching down to a rounded tip with a pad under it, a row of dark plates across its top, and a thick dark claw springing from the top of the tip, forward and hooking down to the ground (the side sheet: big sickle claws, about 0.1 long).

rays.why: Four metacarpal rays continue from the compact wrist/palm to each MCP joint, beneath one hand surface. How to Draw and the SE poster show a broad connected hand, not toe tubes attached to a tapering central point. Outer digits are modestly shorter; the art is oblique, so length scales are conservative design adaptations rather than orthographic measurements.

Four metatarsal rays fan from the raised hock into each MTP joint. Each outer toe needs its own bony/soft-tissue continuation, since the old central ellipsoid ended before its root. The side sheet and How to Draw show a single continuous foot dividing into clawed digits; canine distal-limb references supply the joint hierarchy, not a replacement paw silhouette.
